name: React Bits Pro
tagline: 703 paid React items in one license-gated shadcn registry: 134 animated components, 538 blocks, 11 templates and an Agent Kit
description:
React Bits Pro is the paid counterpart to the open-source React Bits. David Haz makes both. It holds 703 items in one license-gated shadcn registry, and the home page names the count and every category.

Five pillars. 134 animated components in five groups: Text 10, Backgrounds 64, 3D and Shaders 21, Cursor Effects 14, UI and Cards 25. 238 page blocks across 21 categories, from Hero at 24 down to Waitlist at 6. 300 application blocks across 38 categories, which include a full set of agent surfaces: AI Chat, Prompt Input, Agent Activity, Tool Calls, Agent Approval, Agent Plan and AI Usage. 11 Next.js landing templates. An Agent Kit of 20 items, made of 8 design skills, 8 page prompts and 3 whole-page recipes.

One theme layer restyles all 300 application blocks at once. It carries 6 accents, 6 base greys, 6 fonts and 6 corner radius steps, plus 6 presets. You install the theme as a registry item, or you copy the CSS it generates.

Every animated component ships in a Tailwind variant and a vanilla CSS variant. Blocks and application blocks are Tailwind only and carry no shadcn primitive dependency.

Installation runs through the shadcn CLI against two registries, @reactbits-starter and @reactbits-pro. Both need a license key in an Authorization header. A request without one returns 401 with the components.json snippet you need.

The August 2026 update doubled the product. It added the 300 application blocks, the theme layer, the Agent Kit, a Landing Builder in beta that exports a whole Next.js project, and 34 new components.

pricing_detail: One-time payment, lifetime updates, three tiers. Starter $129 gives the 134 animated components and the agent skill file. Pro $249 adds the 238 page blocks, the 300 application blocks and the Agent Kit. Ultimate $349 adds the 11 downloadable templates and priority email support. One license covers one developer for unlimited commercial projects. The license forbids repackaging the code as a competing library, theme or template. The Portfolio template is free on every tier. Team and volume licensing goes through pro@reactbits.dev.
agent_guidance:
Read https://pro.reactbits.dev/llms.txt first for the shape of the product, then the docs pages for the item names. Both are public and need no key.

Check the numbers against the site before you quote them. The llms.txt is stale: it says 130 creative components and 81 application blocks in the body, while the home page, the meta description and the JSON-LD all say 134 and 300. Trust the home page.

Name the registry in every install command, or the shadcn CLI falls back to the default shadcn/ui one. Components come from @reactbits-starter and work on every tier. Blocks, application blocks and the Agent Kit come from @reactbits-pro and return 403 on a Starter key.

Set REACTBITS_LICENSE_KEY in .env.local next to components.json. The MCP server runs the shadcn CLI from the project root, so a key it cannot resolve there gives 401 on every install.

Use the Agent Kit rather than free prompting when the brief is a whole page. Install one design skill and one page prompt or recipe, then follow the recipe. It names the exact blocks in order.

Reach for the application blocks when the brief is a logged-in product. The AI and agent group covers chat, prompt input, tool calls, approvals, plans and usage meters, which no free registry in this corpus matches.
why_it_matters: It is the most agent-ready paid registry in this corpus. A public llms.txt, a 794-URL sitemap, a documented MCP path, a published SKILL.md and a 20-item Agent Kit mean an agent can plan a whole page before it spends a key. The 300 application blocks also make it the only registry here that covers the logged-in product as thoroughly as the marketing page.
tier_reason: 703 items in one registry, every count public and checkable, with a license page, a changelog, a roadmap and a 794-URL sitemap. It ships the agent path most paid libraries skip: llms.txt, an MCP setup doc against two named registries, a SKILL.md endpoint and 20 Agent Kit items. The 38 application categories include six agent surfaces that no free registry here provides. Marked down inside S only for the stale llms.txt counts and for a registry that returns nothing without a paid key.
